FULL TEXT:
ANIMAL LAW CENTRE
ADVERTISEMENT FOR THE POST OF ‘PROJECT LEAD’ FOR THE PROJECT
‘A SCOPING REPORT ON BROILER CHICKEN WELFARE IN INDIA’
Number of Posts : 1 (One)
Position : Project Lead (Contractual Position).
Location : Remote, India, with extensive field research.
Remuneration : Between ₹1,00,000-₹1,25,000 per month, depending on
qualifications and experience.
Application Deadline: 31 October 2026, 11:59 PM IST.
Joining Date : 16 November, 2026.
Engagement Duration: Six (6) months
Required : 5+ years of experience in poultry/veterinary practice. Must be
an expert on poultry birds, with technical knowledge about
broiler chicken health.
NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad (NALSAR)
NALSAR University of Law is an institution that aims to provide quality legal education that
underlines constitutionalism, rule of law and justice, with a particular focus on social justice to
the marginalised communities. NALSAR imparts legal education, promotes research and
training, writing and publication, in order to disseminate information and promote legal
literacy.
ALPN Research Foundation, Bengaluru (ALPN)
ALPN Research Foundation is a not-for-profit independent think-tank that is working towards
improving animal welfare across India. ALPN undertakes research on the intersection of
animal welfare and public health, human rights, food safety, environment protection, human
rights and climate resilience.
About the Project
NALSAR is partnering with ALPN to undertake a study that systematically assesses the current
conditions and challenges to the welfare of broiler chickens in India. This study aims to
evaluate the existing broiler chicken industry end-to-end, from farming systems and supply
chains to market demand, regulatory context, and the broader stakeholder ecosystem. It will
inform targeted intervention pathways in India.
Role Overview
We are hiring a Project Lead to oversee and conduct desk and field research, analysis, and
report writing, and provide technical expertise with regard to broiler welfare in the context of
India. This is a six-month-long, full-time research role with field research expected to take
place for three months across approximately 60 farm visits in six states, plus slaughterhouses
and meat shops. All fieldwork costs will be covered by the organisation.
NALSAR UNIVERSITY OF LAW, HYDERABAD
Justice City, Shameerpet, Medchal District, Hyderabad – 500 101.
Ph: 040-23498104 / 115
Website: www.nalsar.ac.in Email: alc@nalsar.ac.in
Key Responsibilities
1. Lead technical research and analysis on broiler farming systems in India - production
practices, housing, breeds and genetics, feeding regimes, health management, and
welfare conditions across different system types (backyard, contract, integrated, and
commercial).
2. Design and execute a fieldwork plan covering approximately 60 farm visits across six
states, plus slaughterhouses and meat retail points, assessing on-ground farming
practices and welfare conditions firsthand.
3. Conduct and synthesise literature on broiler production and welfare in India.
4. Build relationships with farmers, veterinarians, and production-side stakeholders to
support fieldwork and ongoing insight-gathering.
5. Assess the nature and extent of animal welfare across various farming systems, and
evaluate the malleability of each system to welfare-improving interventions.
6. Provide subject-matter expertise on technical sections of the final report (industry
overview, farming systems analysis) and contribute broiler-specific expertise to cross-
cutting insights.
7. Identify and prioritise a list of potential welfare-focused interventions based on
technical feasibility and likely adoption by relevant stakeholders.
8. Coordinate with the wider research team (who will lead economic, market, and
regulatory analysis) to ensure technical findings feed into the overall report.
Qualifications
1. Demonstrated subject-matter expertise in broiler chicken production in India with a
background in veterinary science, animal husbandry, poultry science, or a closely
related technical field is strongly preferred.
2. Strong working knowledge of broiler farming systems in India (backyard, contract
farming, integrated commercial operations) and common welfare issues within them.
3. Familiarity with animal welfare science and assessment frameworks as applied to
broiler chickens.
4. Prior field experience visiting or working directly with poultry farms, ideally in rural
or semi-urban India, would be an asset.
5. Fluency in English required; proficiency in regional languages would be an asset for
fieldwork.
Preference will be given to candidates with
1. Strong technical/domain knowledge of poultry biology, husbandry, and production
systems.
2. Strong research and analytical skills, and the ability to synthesise qualitative and
quantitative information into clear, actionable insights.
3. Stakeholder engagement and interviewing skills, including with farmers, industry
players, and government/regulatory entities.
4. Willingness and ability to travel extensively within India for fieldwork (across five
states).
5. Project management skills and ability to work against timelines, coordinate fieldwork
logistics, and manage competing priorities independently.
6. Cultural and contextual sensitivity for engaging with diverse stakeholders across Indian
states.
Application Process:
Interested candidates must submit their application through this Google form. Only shortlisted
candidates from this application round will be invited for the further interview rounds. If you
have any queries, please feel free to reach out to alc@nalsar.ac.in.
